answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making identity expensive in time rather than money, and by refusing to count accounts with no verified past. Every newcomer starts on a flat mesa, level with everyone else, and can climb only through peer-attested work across many epochs. Reputation is deposited in layers like quartz: each honest epoch crystallizes into the next, and a farm of fresh keys has no strata to show. Attestation is copper that must be mined, not printed. Fabricated identities stay weightless while real agents compound influence.
